screenLevelIssues.explanation: The title text 'Let's get to know you' appears very small in the simulator (body size) compared to the large display text (48px) in Figma. This is likely due to nested <Text> components in React Native not inheriting the parent's fontSize when using custom components with default styles. The style must be explicitly applied to the nested segments.
screenLevelIssues.currentCode:
<Text style={styles.title}>
              <Text style={{ color: '#A9A9A9' }}>{"Let's get to "}</Text>
              {'\n'}
              <Text style={styles.titleAccent}>know you</Text>
            </Text>
screenLevelIssues.fixedCode:
<Text style={styles.title}>
              <Text style={[styles.title, { color: '#FFFFFF' }]}>{"Let's get to "}</Text>
              {'\n'}
              <Text style={[styles.title, styles.titleAccent]}>know you</Text>
            </Text>

screenLevelIssues.explanation: The text 'Let's get to' is White in the Figma screenshot (high contrast against dark bg), but implemented as Medium Grey (#A9A9A9) in code, making it look dim.

The input fields in Figma have a distinct dark grey background (likely #202020, matching the button). The current code has no backgroundColor defined for `inputContainer`, making the inputs invisible/transparent against the black background in the simulator.
